gloss: to cram; to stuff; to pack in

definitions.explanation: To force many things into a limited space.
To memorize large amounts of information in a short time.

examples.japanese: スーツケースに{荷物|にもつ}を{詰|つ}め{込|こ}んだ。
examples.english: I stuffed the luggage into the suitcase.

examples.japanese: {教室|きょうしつ}に{学生|がくせい}を{詰|つ}め{込|こ}むのは{良|よ}くない。
examples.english: It's not good to cram students into a classroom.

examples.japanese: {小|ちい}さな{車|くるま}に{五人|ごにん}も{詰|つ}め{込|こ}んで{出発|しゅっぱつ}した。
examples.english: We crammed five people into a small car and set off.

examples.japanese: {知識|ちしき}を{頭|あたま}に{詰|つ}め{込|こ}む。
examples.english: To cram knowledge into one's head.

examples.japanese: {試験|しけん}{前|まえ}に{知識|ちしき}を{詰|つ}め{込|こ}んでも、すぐ{忘|わす}れてしまう。
examples.english: Even if you cram knowledge before an exam, you'll forget it quickly.

examples.japanese: {詰|つ}め{込|こ}み{教育|きょういく}ではなく、{考|かんが}える{力|ちから}を{育|そだ}てる{教育|きょういく}が{求|もと}められている。
examples.english: Rather than cramming-style education, education that nurtures the ability to think is being called for.

notes:
{詰|つ}め{込|こ}む is a transitive verb ({他動詞|たどうし}) formed from {詰|つ}める (to pack) + {込|こ}む (into). It implies forcing things in beyond comfortable capacity.

ASPECT (ている):
{詰|つ}め{込|こ}んでいる indicates the state of being crammed full.

PARTICLE PATTERNS:
- [things]を[space]に{詰|つ}め{込|こ}む — to cram [things] into [space]
- [knowledge]を{頭|あたま}に{詰|つ}め{込|こ}む — to cram [knowledge] into one's head

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {鞄|かばん}に{詰|つ}め{込|こ}む (stuff into a bag)
- {知識|ちしき}を{詰|つ}め{込|こ}む (cram knowledge)
- {詰|つ}め{込|こ}み{教育|きょういく} (cramming-style education)

EDUCATIONAL CONTEXT:
{詰|つ}め{込|こ}み{教育|きょういく} refers to rote memorization education, often criticized as superficial learning.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {詰|つ}める: to pack (neutral)
- {押|お}し{込|こ}む: to push/force in
- {詰|つ}め{込|こ}む: to cram (implies excess)
